question.text: Let the coefficients of powers of $x$ in the $2 n d$, 3rd and 4 th terms in the expansion of $(1+x)^{n}$ where $n$ is a positive integer, be in arithmetic progression. Then, the sum of the coefficients of odd powers of $x$ in the expansion is

solution.text:
According to question, ${ }^{n} C_{1},{ }^{n} C_{2}$ and ${ }^{n} C_{3}$ are in $\mathrm{AP}$
$\Rightarrow \quad \frac{2 n(n-1)}{2 !}=n+\frac{n(n-1)(n-2)}{3 !}$
$\Rightarrow \quad n^{2}-9 n+14=0$
$\Rightarrow \quad(n-7)(n-2)=0$
$\Rightarrow \quad n=7$ since $\underline{n \neq 2}$
¿The sum of the coefficients of odd powers of $x$ in the expansion of $(1+x)^{n}$ is $\frac{2^{n}}{2}=\frac{2^{\gamma}}{2}=2^{6}=64$
